title: Convert opaque flag payloads to typed flag contracts and compact rollout history
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: The current feature-flag surface stores semi-structured JSON blobs and string-encoded contract payloads (version tags embedded in arbitrary strings). This makes runtime parsing expensive, causes a proliferation of ad-hoc version checks in the serving runtime, and bloats rollout history with repeated legacy versions. It also complicates audits and automated policy checks.

Goal: Migrate flag storage and runtime handling from opaque string/JSON blobs to a small set of typed, versioned flag contracts with canonical serialization. Compact historical rollout traces into a canonical manifest format and remove stale opcode handling in the runtime after a safe deprecation window. The effort should preserve compatibility for two release cycles while reducing runtime parsing overhead and rollout-history storage by at least 40%.
tasks: Design typed flag contract schemas (YAML + JSON Schema) for the 8 most-used flag types and review with PM/Design/SEC
Implement a compatibility shim in the runtime that accepts both opaque blobs and typed contracts (feature-flag-parser v2)
Write an offline migration tool that scans flags table, validates payloads, translates to typed format, and produces a compact manifest per rollout
Add DB migration to store typed payloads in new columns while leaving legacy_column as read-only for rollback window
Create an admin UI change to show typed contract fields and a migration progress view
Add e2e and unit tests covering parsing, fallback to legacy, and schema validation failures
Run a staged canary: internal service -> small customer cohort -> wide rollout; monitor errors and latency impact
Compact rollout-history: implement background job to collapse repetitive historical entries into canonical manifest and mark older entries as archived
Schedule removal of legacy parsing code two releases after migration completion and add a changelog entry
Document migration steps in Confluence and update runbooks for rollback and incident recovery
acceptance_criteria: Runtime handles typed contracts natively and falls back to legacy blobs without errors for at least 2 release cycles
DB contains new typed_payload column populated for 95% of active flags after migration job runs on staging
End-to-end latency for flag resolution does not regress by more than 5% in p95 compared to baseline
Rollout-history storage for migrated flags is reduced by >=40% after compaction job completes
Admin UI surfaces typed fields and migration progress; product sign-off received
All new unit/e2e tests pass in CI and new integration tests land in nightly runs
risks: Migration may encounter malformed legacy payloads requiring manual remediation (we will capture those in a quarantine list)
Edge-case flags with ad-hoc fields could cause policy mismatches in rollout semantics
Customer workloads depending on opaque encoding for downstream automation might break if we remove legacy support too soon
Large table migration could increase DB write IO and affect peak traffic; plan for rate-limited background migration
rollout_plan: Week 1: Schema design + RFC + security review signoff
Week 2: Implement runtime compatibility shim + unit tests
Week 3: Build migration tool and dry-run on staging snapshot; collect quarantine list
Week 4: Run migration in a controlled internal canary and validate admin UI
Week 5: Open beta for 10% of customers (controlled via routing policy)
Week 6: Full migration for active flags, start rollout-history compaction job
Monitoring: watch flag-resolution errors, p95 latency, admin UI errors, and migration progress dashboard
Post-migration: keep legacy_column readable-only for 2 cycles, then remove parsing code and drop column
